issues.legal_issue: The entire sthanam property held by a sthanamdar passes on death for estate-duty purposes, notwithstanding a per-capita division used to determine its later distribution.
material_facts: The deceased held the sthanam property during his lifetime, subject to restrictions on alienation.
Neither the tarwad members nor the deceased’s personal heirs had an interest in the sthanam property before his death.
The succession arrangement provided for the property to be distributed among the family members and personal heirs by reference to a per-capita division immediately before death.
The estate-duty assessment included the whole sthanam property, while the accountable person contended that only the deceased’s notional per-capita share was chargeable.
issues.conclusion: The whole sthanam property passed on the sthanamdar’s death and was liable to estate duty; the per-capita division determined the shares for distribution and did not limit the property passing to the deceased’s notional share.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 5(1) and 7(1) of the Estate Duty Act, 1953, estate duty is charged on property passing on death, including the benefit arising when the deceased’s interest ceases. Section 7(3) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, makes the sthanam property devolve upon the family members and the sthanamdar’s heirs, with the per-capita division serving to determine their shares for distribution rather than to effect an actual division during the sthanamdar’s lifetime. The Court confined the legal fiction to its purpose of distributing the property and adopted the constitutionally consistent construction, having regard to Article 19(1)(f) and Kavalappara Kottarathil Kochuni v. State of Madras. It also approved the meaning of “devolve” as passing from a person dying to a person living, as stated in Parr v. Parr.

rule.if: estate_duty_assessment and deceased_held_entire_property_during_life and family_and_heirs_had_no_prior_interest and per_capita_division_only_determined_distribution

predicates.estate_duty_assessment: The proceeding concerns an assessment of estate duty on property held by a person who died.
predicates.deceased_held_entire_property_during_lif: The deceased held the whole property during life, subject to any restrictions on dealing with it.
predicates.family_and_heirs_had_no_prior_interest: The deceased’s family members and personal heirs had no interest in the property before the deceased died.
predicates.per_capita_division_only_determined_dist: The arrangement treated the property as divided per capita to determine the shares distributed to family members and heirs, without dividing the deceased’s lifetime interest.

issues.definition: When an estate-duty assessment concerns property held entirely by the deceased, the family and heirs had no prior interest in it, and a per-capita division only determines its distribution, the whole property passes on death and is chargeable to estate duty.
